```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

pkginspectr answers simple questions about R packages: how many files, tests
and help pages does a package have, and how many of its lines are code,
comments or documentation? It works on local folders, GitHub repositories and
CRAN packages, returns tidy tibbles, and draws bar charts right in the console.

```{r setup}
library(pkginspectr)
```

## A package to play with

pkginspectr ships a tiny example package so you can try everything offline.
`pkginspectr_example()` returns its path:

```{r}
example <- pkginspectr_example()
```

Every function below takes a `path`. It can be:

* a local folder, such as `"."` for the package you are working on,
* a GitHub repository, such as `"r-lib/cli"`, or
* the name of a CRAN package, such as `"desc"`.

Remote packages can be pinned to a version, and prefixes make the source
explicit:

| `path`                          | Meaning                                   |
|---------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| `"r-lib/cli@v3.6.0"`            | GitHub tag, branch or commit              |
| `"github::apache/arrow/r"`      | A package in a subfolder of a repository  |
| `"cran::desc@1.4.0"`            | An older CRAN release                     |
| `"local::pkgs/mypkg"`           | A local folder, never looked up online    |

GitHub and CRAN packages are downloaded once and cached for the rest of the R
session. With `cache = "persistent"`, fixed versions (CRAN releases, GitHub
tags and commits) are kept across sessions too. `pkg_cache_clear()` empties
the cache.

## Files and folders: `pkg_structure()`

```{r}
pkg_structure(example)
```

`num_r_files` counts the scripts in `R/`, split into files that define at
least one function and files that do not. `num_test_files` counts R files
under `tests/`.

## Lines of code: `pkg_lines()`

```{r}
lines <- pkg_lines(example)
lines
```

The columns break `total_lines` down in two ways, and each adds up to the
total:

* **by type**: `code_lines`, `comment_lines`, `roxygen_lines` and
  `blank_lines`;
* **by location**: `r_lines` (in `R/`), `test_lines` (in `tests/`) and
  `other_lines` (e.g. `data-raw/`).

```{r}
with(lines, code_lines + comment_lines + roxygen_lines + blank_lines)
with(lines, r_lines + test_lines + other_lines)
```

`function_lines` counts the code lines inside function definitions, so it is
part of `code_lines`.

Lines are classified with R's own parser rather than pattern matching. A `#`
inside a string is not a comment, a `{` inside a string does not open a
block, and functions are found however they are written: with `<-`, with `=`,
as `\(x)` lambdas, or as anonymous functions passed to other calls.

## Everything at once: `pkg_summary()`

`pkg_summary()` combines both tables. For GitHub or CRAN packages it downloads
each package only once, so it is the quickest way to get everything:

```{r}
pkg_summary(example)
```

## What gets counted

pkginspectr counts the files that `R CMD build` would put into the package
tarball. It skips version-control folders such as `.git/`, R's standard
exclusions such as `.Rproj.user/` and `.Rhistory`, and anything listed in the
package's `.Rbuildignore`, which often includes `docs/` and `data-raw/`.

This matters when comparing packages: a local checkout and the CRAN release of
the same package give comparable numbers. To count `.Rbuildignore`d files as
well, use `include_ignored = TRUE`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pkg_lines(".", include_ignored = TRUE)
```

## Plotting in the console

`pkg_plot()`, or simply `plot()`, draws bar charts in the console. The default
view shows one panel per package, with each metric as a share of its total:

```{r}
plot(lines)
```

With several packages, `type = "metric"` shows one panel per metric instead,
with bars scaled to the largest value:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pkg_summary(c("r-lib/cli", "r-lib/fs", "desc")) |>
  pkg_plot(type = "metric")
```

Bars are plain characters, so you can restyle them:

```{r}
pkg_plot(
  lines,
  bar_col = "darkorange",
  glyph = "=",
  start = "[",
  end = "]",
  max_bars = 20,
  title = "examplepkg at a glance"
)
```

## Quiet mode

All functions report progress as they go. Use `quiet = TRUE` to turn the
messages off, for example in scripts or reports:

```{r}
pkg_lines(example, quiet = TRUE)
```
